statements.says: An individual labour dispute is any disagreement between an employee and an employer about performing the employment relationship, if not resolved by internal settlement.
Every individual labour dispute must be the subject of a conciliation attempt before the conciliation office before any court action is started.
Conciliation is optional when the defendant lives outside the country, or in a case of bankruptcy or judicial settlement of the employer.
Individual disputes involving civil servants and agents under the basic statute of public institutions and administrations are outside the conciliation offices' competence.
Collective agreements may set internal procedures for handling individual labour disputes inside the employing body.
Absent such procedures, the worker raises the matter with the direct superior (8 days to answer), then the management or employer, who must answer in writing within 15 days.
After internal procedures are exhausted, the worker may notify the labour inspector.
The labour inspectorate is notified for the conciliation attempt by written petition or by the plaintiff in person, in which case the inspector records his statements.
The inspector passes the notification to the conciliation office within three days and summons the parties, with at least 8 days between summons and meeting.
The office may strike the case if the plaintiff or representative does not attend without serious and lawful excuse; the plaintiff is told within 8 days.
If the defendant does not attend, he is summoned again for a meeting within 8 days at most.
If the defendant is absent from two consecutive meetings, the office draws up a record of non-conciliation and a copy is given to the plaintiff during the meeting.
If the parties agree on all or part of the dispute, the office draws up a conciliation record.
If the parties do not agree, the office draws up a record of non-conciliation.
The conciliation record is proof unless challenged as forged.
In case of non-conciliation, the interested party brings an action before the court deciding social matters.
The petition to the court is accompanied by a copy of the non-conciliation record issued by the conciliation office.
The first hearing is set within 15 days following the date the opening petition is sent.
Social-matter courts hear individual labour disputes arising from performance, suspension or termination of an employment, training or apprenticeship relationship.

The action is brought where the employment relationship is performed or where the defendant resides; where the plaintiff resides if the suspension or break results from a work accident or occupational disease.
The social section has exclusive jurisdiction over proof and performance, suspension and termination of employment, training and apprenticeship contracts.

Territorial jurisdiction lies with the court of the place where the contract was concluded or performed, or of the defendant's domicile; the plaintiff's domicile if termination or suspension is due to a work accident or occupational disease.
The social section sits as a judge-president with assessors as labour legislation provides, on pain of nullity.
The action before the social section is brought by an opening petition under the ordinary rules.
The action must be filed within 6 months from delivery of the non-conciliation record, on pain of forfeiture of the right to sue.
The first hearing is set within 15 days of filing.
Additional claims following from the main claim are admitted at every stage even if not subject of a conciliation attempt.

priorSteps.requiredWhen: Every individual labour dispute (employee v. employer on performing the employment relationship), before any court action; the non-conciliation record is then attached to the petition (art. 37) and the action filed within 6 months of its delivery.
notRequiredWhen: Conciliation is optional where the defendant resides outside the national territory (labour-disputes 19 para 2)
Conciliation is optional in case of bankruptcy or judicial settlement of the employer (labour-disputes 19 para 2)
Disputes of civil servants and agents under the basic statute of public institutions and administrations are outside the offices' competence (labour-disputes 19 para 3)

priorSteps.requiredWhen: Internal settlement inside the employing body (collective agreement procedure, or direct superior then management) is the route before notifying the inspector; whether it is a condition of filing is not stated.

sections.matter: Individual labour disputes; proof, performance, suspension, termination of employment, training and apprenticeship contracts (exclusive jurisdiction)
Immediate enforcement of conciliation agreement, and interim or protective measures against acts obstructing freedom to work, before the president of the social section

territory.rule: Court of the place where the employment contract was concluded or performed, or of the defendant's domicile
Court of the place where the employment relationship is performed or the defendant resides

territory.when: Termination or suspension of the employment due to a work accident or occupational disease

exits.when: Disputes of civil servants and agents under the basic statute of public institutions and administrations are excluded from the conciliation offices; the texts given do not say which court hears them

openPoints.question: Is a missing conciliation (no non-conciliation record attached) a bar to the action?
readings: Art. 19 para 1 and art. 37 make it a mandatory precondition, though no text given states a sanction
No sanction is stated for labour (unlike cpca 536 bis 4 para 3 for commercial courts), so the action may not be barred

openPoints.question: What starts the 6 months in cpca 504 when the record was handed over at the meeting (labour-disputes 30 para 2) or sent later?
readings: The date of handing over at the meeting
The date of actual delivery to the plaintiff if later

openPoints.question: How is the 6-month period counted (first/last day, non-working day)?
readings: No text given says; counting rule is missing from these texts

openPoints.question: Who may raise the forfeiture of cpca 504?
readings: The court of its own motion
Only a party

openPoints.question: Does the 6-month period apply where conciliation was optional (art. 19 para 2) so no record exists?
readings: The period cannot start without a record
The period does not apply but a general time limit may

openPoints.question: Scope of the optional conciliation: does 'حالة الإفلاس أو تسوية قضائية' cover bankruptcy of the employer only?
readings: Employer only (as read in the text)
Any bankruptcy or settlement affecting the defendant

openPoints.question: Are the internal procedures of arts. 3 to 5 a condition before conciliation or filing?
readings: Art. 5 says 'can notify', so optional
They must be exhausted first

openPoints.question: Where do disputes of public officials go?
readings: Administrative court (not stated in the texts)
Another section

openPoints.question: Which territorial rule prevails when cpca 501 (place of conclusion or performance, or domicile) and labour-disputes 24 (place of performance or residence) differ?
readings: Both give options; the plaintiff may choose among all places
Law 90-04 art. 24 specific, so conclusion place is not available

openPoints.question: A partial agreement (art. 31 para 1): is a non-conciliation record issued for the rest and does the 6-month period run?
readings: A record of partial conciliation is issued and the remainder needs a non-conciliation record
Texts silent

openPoints.question: Date for the first hearing: from filing (cpca 505) or from sending the petition (labour-disputes 38)?
readings: Filing date
Date the petition is directed to the court
